examples.title: Balanced ANOVA from means and SDs
examples.prompt: Postmenopausal women were randomized to three treatment groups (\(n = 12\) each) and their rate of bone loss was measured for 2 years. Is there a difference in the rate of bone loss among these three groups? Use \(\alpha = 0.05\), and if a difference exists do not identify which groups are different.

steps.say: The test is analysis of variance (there are more than two groups made of different subjects, and the data are interval and Normally distributed).
The null hypothesis is that there is no difference in the mean rate of bone loss among women in these three treatment groups.
There are three groups and 12 women in each group.
These are the general equations, written before any numbers go in, because each one earns credit on its own.
Square each SD and average the three squares. This gives the within-groups variance.
Average the three group means to get the grand mean. Then find how far each group mean sits from it and turn that into a variance.
Multiply by the 12 women per group. This gives the between-groups variance.
Divide the between-groups variance by the within-groups variance.
The numerator uses the number of groups minus 1. The denominator uses the 11 free values in each of the three groups.
Row 33 is not printed in the F table, so the cutoff sits between rows 32 and 34 in the column for 2. Lightface numbers give 0.05 and boldface numbers give 0.01.
F is larger than both cutoffs, so reject the null hypothesis. There is a difference in the mean rate of bone loss among women in these three treatment groups, with P less than 0.01.
The question says not to identify which groups are different, so the answer ends with the overall conclusion and no pairwise tests.

examples.title: Read an R aov table
examples.prompt: 165 subjects with raised BNP levels were randomly assigned to a placebo, an experimental drug or the standard treatment (55 per group). R gives this ANOVA output from aov(BNP ~ Group). Read the table and state the result.

steps.say: The Group row has Df 2, which is the numerator degrees of freedom because there are three groups.
The Residuals row has Df 162 and Mean Sq 2075. These are the within degrees of freedom and the within-groups variance.
F is 11.49 and P is \(2.16\times10^{-5}\), so reject the null hypothesis. There is a difference in BNP levels among the three treatment groups, with P less than 0.001.
Keep 2075 as the within-groups variance with 162 degrees of freedom, because any pairwise t tests after this ANOVA reuse them.
